2608.23045.title: From Inertia to Objectivity: Improving Deep Research Agents with Noise Isolation
2608.23045.paper_summary: Web search agents powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) show strong promise, but deep research tasks expose a recurring failure mode: once an agent has produced a query, plan, or intermediate conclusion, it becomes less objective when later judging the consequences of that same action. We term this phenomenon \textbf{inertia bias}. To make it measurable, we introduce the IBIS benchmark, which controls the search observations while varying whether the model is evaluating the outcome of its own prior action. We find that models are substantially worse when they ``own'' the preceding search step, showing that self-authored action history can systematically distort subsequent judgment. We further show that this bias propagates into two forms of system-level degradation: search noise at the worker level and contextual noise at the manager level. To address this problem, we propose NIS-Agent, which applies context isolation at the two decision points most vulnerable to inertia bias: webpage triage and final-answer validation. Across GAIA, WebWalkerQA, BrowseComp, and BrowseComp-zh, NIS-Agent achieves competitive performance while reducing token cost by 33\% compared to our baseline. We further train an 8B model to be intrinsically more resistant to inertia bias; under the same NIS-Agent framework, it attains average performance comparable to GPT-4o on deep research benchmarks.
2608.23045.paper_summary_zh: 網路搜尋代理商由大型語言模型（LLMs）驅動，顯示出強大的潛力，但深入的研究任務暴露出一種反覆出現的失敗模式：一旦代理商產生了查詢、計劃或中間結論，在隨後評估該行動的後果時，它變得不那麼客觀。我們將這種現象稱為\textbf{慣性偏見}。為了使其可衡量，我們引入了IBIS基準，該基準在變化模型是否評估其自身先前行動的結果時，控制搜尋觀察。我們發現，當模型“擁有”先前的搜尋步驟時，其性能顯著下降，顯示自我創作的行動歷史可以系統性地扭曲後續的判斷。我們進一步顯示，這種偏見會傳播到兩種系統層級的退化形式：工作層級的搜尋噪音和管理層級的上下文噪音。為了解決這個問題，我們提出了NIS-Agent，它在最容易受到慣性偏見影響的兩個決策點上應用上下文隔離：網頁分類和最終答案驗證。在GAIA、WebWalkerQA、BrowseComp和BrowseComp-zh中，NIS-Agent在降低33\%的標記成本的同時，達到了與我們的基準相當的競爭性能。我們進一步訓練了一個8B模型，使其在慣性偏見上具內在的更高抗性；在相同的NIS-Agent框架下，它在深度研究基準上達到了與GPT-4o相當的平均性能。
